no_intercity_link.rule: ONE hub, TWO independent clusters. There is NO Miami↔Fort Lauderdale water link in ANY phase — do not render, imply, or reserve a connector line between the clusters.
no_intercity_link.reason: Inventory verdict: ~25–30 nm either routing; inside (ICW) hits the winter-slow Sunny Isles/Dumbfoundling segment, bridge idle pockets, and the Port Everglades slow zone (90+ min winter); outside (ocean) hits the Government Cut slow RNA exit, ~20 nm open-Atlantic sea-state exposure (ops gate unverified), and the Port Everglades slow entry (~60–75 min best case). Brightline already serves the city-pair in ~30–40 min — the water product cannot beat it on time.
no_intercity_link.revisit_conditions: Only if (a) an anchor employer pre-commits both ends, and (b) the vessel's offshore sea-state envelope is proven.

lines.phase_notes: Flagship — the strongest single corridor found in any city scanned to date. ~6 nm ≈ 20–25 min, foil-credible year-round, vs 80–90 min crisis-era Rickenbacker drives on the island's only road. Crandon is park-&-ride ($181.5K median HH income catchment); the entire Brickell finance cluster is within 12 min of the Vice City dock. Time claim (20–25 min) is whitelisted.

lines.name: Grove Line

segments.routing: Open bay with 1000-ft slow-speed shore buffers at each end; ~4.5–5 nm.

segments.constraint: Slow-speed all year around Brickell Key + river-mouth idle/slow zone on the EPIC approach (short hop)
segments.routing: Bayside only — EPIC's bay face; never enter the Miami River (idle all year + drawbridge curfews).

lines.phase_notes: Dinner Key ↔ Brickell in 15–20 min (foil-credible year-round; time claim whitelisted for this leg only) with City Hall + Grove offices southbound as reverse-commute demand. The short EPIC extension is the second Brickell gate serving the Flagler St downtown edge — that hop is speed-constrained and gets NO time claim.

lines.name: Beach Line

segments.routing: MANDATORY: exit Miami Beach Marina through the Government Cut RNA slow water (~0.5–1 nm), then via NORRIS CUT to open bay at speed. NEVER route via Fisherman's Channel (USCG slow RNA). No geometry through or over Fisher Island.

lines.phase_notes: SoFi premium catchment to Brickell finance jobs, ~5.5 nm ≈ 20–25 min via Norris Cut (foil-credible with routing care; time claim whitelisted). Complements — does not fight — the city's free Sunset Harbour↔Venetian water taxi.

lines.name: North Bay Line

segments.routing: Designated 30/35-mph channels and unzoned mid-bay water; idle pockets at the 79th St bridge.

segments.constraint: Downtown ICW channel is IDLE SPEED all year from 100 yd N of Venetian Cswy to the southern tip of Brickell Key — fixed slow tail into downtown

lines.phase_notes: Uses the 30/35-mph mid-bay water; accepts the idle tail into downtown. Pelican↔Venetian leg is time-claim eligible (30-mph ICW whitelist); the downtown tail renders indicative only.

lines.name: Gold Coast Line

segments.routing: 30-mph all-year ICW segments + unzoned mid-bay; several bridge idle pockets.

segments.constraint: Downtown ICW channel idle-speed all year (Venetian Cswy → Brickell Key) — fixed slow tail

lines.name: Bay Line

Copy may cite the city service's 20-minute crossing as public proof; NO Navier time claim for this line until geometry seals (not on the foil-credible whitelist). Requires a City of Miami Beach dock agreement at Maurice Gibb (internal only).

segments.routing: ICW channel; transit the Port Everglades entrance channel at posted speed (security-sensitive port — internal).

segments.routing: ICW to New River junction, then upriver past the 3rd Ave and Andrews Ave drawbridges (opening-rule schedule risk — internal open item).

catchment_counting_rule: stations_at_launch / stations_full_network = count of OTHER stations reachable from the anchor's station via authored lines (transfers allowed at interchanges), at Phase 1 vs all phases, WITHIN the anchor's cluster only — never across clusters (no intercity link exists). The Miami cluster contains two deliberately separate sub-networks with no authored water link between their hubs: the Brickell group (vice-city-marina, epic-marina, crandon-key-biscayne, dinner-key-grove, miami-beach-marina — 5 stations, all Phase 1, so 4 reachable at launch and at full network) and the north-bay group (venetian-marina, miamarina-bayside, sunset-harbour, pelican-harbor, bill-bird-haulover, aventura-loggerhead — 6 stations, all Phase 2, so 0 at launch and 5 at full network; aventura-loggerhead counts but is summer-season only). The Fort Lauderdale cluster is one connected network: 4 Phase-1 stations (3 reachable at launch) growing to 5 (4 reachable at full network).

speed_zone_honesty.rule: Segments flagged speed_constrained:true must render water_min as 'indicative — subject to local speed zones'. Crossing-time claims appear ONLY on corridors the inventory marks foil-credible: Island Line (20–25 min), Grove Line Dinner Key↔Brickell leg (15–20 min), Beach Line via Norris Cut (20–25 min), and the north-bay 30-mph ICW legs (Pelican↔Venetian, Bill Bird↔Venetian). Everything else — all FTL legs, all downtown-idle tails, the EPIC hop, the Bay Line, Aventura — renders indicative with no bare numbers.
constrained_zones: Miami River — IDLE speed all year, entire river (plus drawbridge curfews, 33 CFR 117.305) — never route service upriver
Downtown ICW channel — IDLE speed all year, 100 yd N of Venetian Cswy → southern tip of Brickell Key; slow-speed all year around Brickell Key
Government Cut & Fisherman's Channel — USCG Regulated Navigation Area, slow speed for vessels <50 m (effective Jan 29 2025)
Port Everglades — slow speed in ALL port waters year-round + 6,000-ft ICW idle zone Nov 15–Mar 31
New River — slow speed all year, both forks, through downtown Fort Lauderdale
Sunny Isles / Dumbfoundling Bay ICW — channel slow-speed Nov 15–Apr 30 (Aventura seasonal gate)
Year-round slow-speed BRA, ICW between Oakland Park Blvd and Sunrise Blvd bridges (FWC, Nov 2025)
speed_zone_honesty.note: FWC manatee zones regulate speed/wake, not hull type — a zero-wake hydrofoil gets NO automatic exemption from posted zones. FWC + Miami-Dade DERM engagement is the #1 regulatory workstream; the Miami-Dade Manatee Protection Plan is being updated now. Do not soften this in copy.

no_intercity_link.rule: NO Miami↔Fort Lauderdale water link in any phase — do not render, imply, or reserve a connector. The two clusters are independent networks (25–30 nm, hard slow segments both routings, Brightline wins on time). Zero cross-cluster segments in geometry.

incumbent_respect.rule: Water Taxi FTL owns leisure hours (10:00–22:00) — Navier's FTL positioning is the unserved commuter blocks (6:30–9:30 / 16:30–19:00), as a complement, potentially using their docks under agreement. Never disparage or position as displacement. The free Miami Beach city water taxi (live since Jan 20 2026, Sunset Harbour ↔ Venetian, 20 min) is a PUBLIC PROOF POINT — copy may say 'Miami Beach already runs a commuter water taxi — we make it a network' and may cite its 20-min crossing. Never imply Navier replaces the free city service; the premium pitch is frequency, reach (Brickell/Key Biscayne/Grove), and guaranteed employer seats.

maurice_gibb_agreement_internal_only.rule: The Maurice Gibb dock is the City of Miami Beach's contracted water-taxi dock (incumbent operator holds the contract via city RFQ); Navier service there requires a city agreement. This lives in note_internal only — never rendered.

hurricane_season_internal_only.rule: Hurricane-season ops (Jun 1–Nov 30 exposure, haul-out/berthing contingencies, service-suspension protocol) and the winter manatee-season/peak-demand overlap are internal planning material — never rendered in copy.

aventura_seasonal_honesty.rule: Aventura renders as a seasonal station with the honest regulatory reason visible: 'summer season only (May 1–Nov 14) — the Intracoastal channel here is a slow-speed manatee zone Nov 15–Apr 30'. Do NOT use resort/summer-premium framing; the season is set by rule, not by demand.

gates.no_invented_landings: Every stop maps to the exact named landing in MIAMI-NODE-INVENTORY.md. Any stop that cannot be ID-matched to a real BP goes to the bp_gap ledger with reason and renders only from inventory-named coordinates — never guess.
gates.times_indicative: ALL times marked indicative until Atlas geometry seals them; whitelisted claims render with the inventory's ranges and an 'indicative' qualifier.
gates.loi_framing: Non-binding letter of intent — a seat-block interest signal, not a purchase.
gates.no_dock_negotiation_language: No copy about dock deals, berthing negotiations, city agreements, marina terms, or landing diligence (incl. the Vice City berthing question) — internal only.
gates.launch_timing: Service launch not before end-2027. All network rendering is coverage narrative, not a service promise; seat economics still gate corridor launch (60–80 committed seats).

copy.hero: Key Biscayne to Brickell in 20–25 minutes — instead of an 80–90 minute causeway crawl. Navier is building an employer water network for South Florida: 20-seat electric hydrofoils linking Key Biscayne, Coconut Grove, and South Beach to a dock two minutes from Brickell's towers, plus a second network connecting Hollywood Beach and the Las Olas Isles to downtown Fort Lauderdale.

sections.why_miami: Miami's jobs sit on the water and its commutes sit in traffic. Brickell — the densest finance cluster in the Southeast — is a two-minute walk from an existing marina, and Key Biscayne's only road home has meant 80–90 minute drives. Miami Beach already runs a commuter water taxi — a free city service crossing the bay in a consistent 20 minutes since January 2026. We make it a network: more corridors, commuter frequency, and guaranteed employer seats.
sections.how_it_works: Employers commit seat blocks on a corridor. When a corridor reaches 60–80 committed seats, it launches. Seats are guaranteed, quiet, working commutes on zero-emission electric hydrofoils.
sections.network_miami: Three launch lines converge on Brickell: the Island Line (Key Biscayne ↔ Brickell, 20–25 min), the Grove Line (Coconut Grove ↔ Brickell, 15–20 min, continuing to the downtown river mouth), and the Beach Line (South Beach ↔ Brickell, 20–25 min). Phase 2 adds a north-bay group — Sunset Harbour, Edgewater, Downtown/Bayside, the Upper Eastside, and Bal Harbour — rendered as planned, not promised.
sections.network_fort_lauderdale: Fort Lauderdale is its own network: the Hollywood Commuter (Hollywood Beach ↔ 17th St ↔ downtown Riverwalk) and the Isles Shuttle (Bahia Mar ↔ Riverwalk) put the Las Olas office spine and the county government center a short walk from the dock. Fort Lauderdale's beloved Water Taxi runs 10 AM to 10 PM — we serve the commuter hours it doesn't, as a complement, not a competitor.
sections.two_networks: Miami and Fort Lauderdale operate as two independent networks. There is no boat between them — Brightline already does that trip in about 35 minutes, and we won't pretend water beats rail there.
sections.aventura_note: Aventura joins as a summer-season station (May–mid-November): the Intracoastal channel there is a slow-speed manatee-protection zone from November 15 to April 30, so foil-speed service pauses each winter. We'd rather tell you that now than surprise you later.
sections.timing: Targeting first service no earlier than end-2027. Every travel time shown is indicative until routes are finalized with harbor and wildlife authorities, and times only appear on corridors where full-speed water is verified.
sections.loi_ask: Register interest with a non-binding letter of intent. It costs nothing and reserves nothing — it tells us which corridors to launch first.
